title: From Docket Minutes to Case Trajectories: Building Analysis-Ready Criminal Court Data
abstract: arXiv:2611.23537v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Criminal court records are often fragmented, noisy, and siloed, making it challenging for both legal experts and community stakeholders to access and analyze court data to identify trends and provide public oversight. In this paper, we introduce a system for data ingestion, harmonization, and dashboard visualization designed for New Orleans criminal court proceedings data, aimed at both expert and lay audiences. Our system collects and harmonizes disparate data, generates case trajectories, and provides intuitive visualization techniques based on community feedback to analyze demographics, temporal trends, and specific case events. We demonstrate the system through an exploratory analysis of recent short-term trends and policy impacts within New Orleans, illustrating how it can support the investigation of anomalies, policy changes, and procedural irregularities. translated_title: 从庭审笔录到案件轨迹：构建可分析就绪的刑事法院数据
translated_abstract: 刑事法院记录往往零碎、嘈杂且相互孤立，这使得法律专家和社区利益相关者都难以访问和分析法院数据以识别趋势并开展公众监督。在本文中，我们介绍了一个面向新奥尔良刑事法院庭审数据的数据摄取、协调与仪表板可视化系统，旨在同时服务专业人士和普通大众。我们的系统收集并协调分散的数据源，生成案件轨迹，并基于社区反馈提供直观的可视化技术，用于分析人口统计特征、时间趋势和具体案件事件。我们通过对新奥尔良近期短期趋势和政策影响的探索性分析来展示该系统，说明其如何支持对异常情况、政策变化和程序违规问题的调查。我们还展示了来自社区利益相关者小型形成性研究的反馈。
tldr: 本文提出一个面向新奥尔良刑事法院数据的数据摄取、协调与可视化仪表板系统，通过生成案件轨迹帮助专家和普通民众分析法院趋势、调查政策影响并实现公众监督。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a data ingestion, harmonization, and dashboard visualization system for New Orleans criminal court proceedings that generates case trajectories, enabling both experts and community stakeholders to analyze trends, investigate policy impacts, and conduct public oversight.
